title: The Raven and the Goose
subtitle: A short story about colour and stubbornness

learningObjectives.text: What does Goose do after Raven complains about the pattern?
What kind of story is this passage?

colours.author: Greenlandic storytellers, collected by Knud Rasmussen
colours.locator: The Raven And The Goose; The Raven And The Goose, normalized characters 144-698
colours.excerpt: It happened in the days when all the birds were getting their colours and the pattern in their coats. And the raven and the goose happened to meet, and they agreed to paint each other. The raven began, and painted the other black, with a nice white pattern showing between. The goose thought that very fine indeed, and began to do the same by the raven, painting it a coat exactly like its own. But then the raven fell into a rage, and declared the pattern was frightfully ugly, and the goose, offended at all the fuss, simply splashed it black all over.
colours.note: Verbatim English rendering by Worster from stories collected by Rasmussen in Greenland. The book title uses an outdated ethnonym; this lesson identifies the collection's Greenland scope.

narrativeBlocks.title: Two birds agree to paint
narrativeBlocks.body: In this story, Raven and Goose agree to paint each other's feathers while birds are receiving their colours and patterns.

narrativeBlocks.title: The painting goes wrong
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from the cited Worster translation (whitespace normalized): “It happened in the days when all the birds were getting their colours and the pattern in their coats. And the raven and the goose happened to meet, and they agreed to paint each other. The raven began, and painted the other black, with a nice white pattern showing between. The goose thought that very fine indeed, and began to do the same by the raven, painting it a coat exactly like its own. But then the raven fell into a rage, and declared the pattern was frightfully ugly, and the goose, offended at all the fuss, simply splashed it black all over.”

narrativeBlocks.title: The source offers an explanation
narrativeBlocks.body: The story says Raven becomes angry about the pattern Goose paints, and Goose responds by splashing Raven all over with black.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not turn a story into natural history
narrativeBlocks.body: This is a narrative in Rasmussen's Greenland collection, not a zoological account or a claim that every Inuit group tells this exact bird story.

narrativeBlocks.title: A just-so ending
narrativeBlocks.body: The final line links Raven's black colour to the quarrel in this tale.
